why: Same conclusion on both sides (sc-smooth f : X -> [0,1], f(x) = 1, tsupport f ⊆ U, f = 1 near x), same setting (no tameness). The only difference is the hypothesis: A (proposition_5_5_3 / proposition_5_3_2, universe 0) assumes AdmitsBumpFunctions (a bump with f(x) != 0, the project's reading of Def. 5.9), B assumes AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak (the literal 'not identically zero' of Def. 5.29). B => A by AdmitsBumpFunctions.weak. A => B would need weak bumps to give a bump non-zero at the given point; on an M-polyfold there are no translations (translation by a non-smooth point is not sc^0 on the levels), so this is a genuine strengthening of the hypothesis, not glue, and B's truth in general is unclear (the blind author flagged the same doubt). A is exactly B's BStrong (proved both ways).
overlap: 109 shared project theorems, all proof fields/infrastructure of realPolyfold/realChart and the sc-calculus reached through the statement types; nothing from the proof of Prop 5.30 (smoothTransition composition) is reused.
intended: A <-> BStrong proved in both directions (A_to_BStrong, BStrong_to_A).
